NNAAMMEE
       jwebserver - launch the Java Simple Web Server

SSYYNNOOPPSSIISS
       jjwweebbsseerrvveerr [_o_p_t_i_o_n_s]

       _o_p_t_i_o_n_s
              Command-line options.  For a detailed description of the options, see OOppttiioonnss.

DDEESSCCRRIIPPTTIIOONN
       The  jjwweebbsseerrvveerr  tool provides a minimal HTTP server, designed to be used for prototyping,
       testing, and debugging.  It serves a single directory hierarchy, and  only  serves  static
       files.  Only HTTP/1.1 is supported; HTTP/2 and HTTPS are not supported.

       Only  idempotent HEAD and GET requests are served.  Any other requests receive a 550011 -- NNoott
       IImmpplleemmeenntteedd or a 440055 -- NNoott AAlllloowweedd response.  GET requests are mapped to the directory be-
       ing served, as follows:

       +o If the requested resource is a file, its content is served.

       +o If the requested resource is a directory that contains an index file, the content of the
         index file is served.

       +o Otherwise, the names of all files and subdirectories of the directory are listed.   Sym-
         bolic links and hidden files are not listed or served.

       MIME  types  are  configured  automatically, using the built-in table.  For example, ..hhttmmll
       files are served as tteexxtt//hhttmmll and ..jjaavvaa files are served as tteexxtt//ppllaaiinn.

       jjwweebbsseerrvveerr is located in the jdk.httpserver module, and can alternatively be started  with
       jjaavvaa   --mm   jjddkk..hhttttppsseerrvveerr.   It  is  based  on  the  web  server  implementation  in  the
       ccoomm..ssuunn..nneett..hhttttppsseerrvveerr package.  The  ccoomm..ssuunn..nneett..hhttttppsseerrvveerr..SSiimmpplleeFFiilleeSSeerrvveerr  class  pro-
       vides  a  programmatic  way to retrieve the server and its components for reuse and exten-
       sion.

UUSSAAGGEE
              jjwweebbsseerrvveerr [[--bb bbiinndd aaddddrreessss]] [[--pp ppoorrtt]] [[--dd ddiirreeccttoorryy]]
                         [[--oo nnoonnee||iinnffoo||vveerrbboossee]] [[--hh ttoo sshhooww ooppttiioonnss]]
                         [[--vveerrssiioonn ttoo sshhooww vveerrssiioonn iinnffoorrmmaattiioonn]]

OOPPTTIIOONNSS
       --hh or --?? or ----hheellpp
              Prints the help message and exits.

       --bb _a_d_d_r or ----bbiinndd--aaddddrreessss _a_d_d_r
              Specifies the address to bind to.  Default: 127.0.0.1 or ::1 (loopback).   For  all
              interfaces use --bb 00..00..00..00 or --bb ::::.

       --dd _d_i_r or ----ddiirreeccttoorryy _d_i_r
              Specifies the directory to serve.  Default: current directory.

       --oo _l_e_v_e_l or ----oouuttppuutt _l_e_v_e_l
              Specifies the output format.  nnoonnee | iinnffoo | vveerrbboossee.  Default: iinnffoo.

       --pp _p_o_r_t or ----ppoorrtt _p_o_r_t
              Specifies the port to listen on.  Default: 8000.

       --vveerrssiioonn or ----vveerrssiioonn
              Prints the version information and exits.

       To stop the server, press CCttrrll ++ CC.

SSTTAARRTTIINNGG TTHHEE SSEERRVVEERR
       The following command starts the Simple Web Server:

              $$ jjwweebbsseerrvveerr

       If  startup is successful, the server prints a message to SSyysstteemm..oouutt listing the local ad-
       dress and the absolute path of the directory being served.  For example:

              $$ jjwweebbsseerrvveerr
              BBiinnddiinngg ttoo llooooppbbaacckk bbyy ddeeffaauulltt.. FFoorr aallll iinntteerrffaacceess uussee ""--bb 00..00..00..00"" oorr ""--bb ::::""..
              SSeerrvviinngg //ccwwdd aanndd ssuubbddiirreeccttoorriieess oonn 112277..00..00..11 ppoorrtt 88000000
              UURRLL hhttttpp::////112277..00..00..11::88000000//

CCOONNFFIIGGUURRAATTIIOONN
       By default, the server runs in the foreground and binds to the loopback address  and  port
       8000.   This  can  be changed with the --bb and --pp options.  For example, to bind the Simple
       Web Server to all interfaces, use:

              $$ jjwweebbsseerrvveerr --bb 00..00..00..00
              SSeerrvviinngg //ccwwdd aanndd ssuubbddiirreeccttoorriieess oonn 00..00..00..00 ((aallll iinntteerrffaacceess)) ppoorrtt 88000000
              UURRLL hhttttpp::////112233..445566..77..889911::88000000//

       Note that this makes the web server accessible to all hosts on the  network.   _D_o  _n_o_t  _d_o
       _t_h_i_s _u_n_l_e_s_s _y_o_u _a_r_e _s_u_r_e _t_h_e _s_e_r_v_e_r _c_a_n_n_o_t _l_e_a_k _a_n_y _s_e_n_s_i_t_i_v_e _i_n_f_o_r_m_a_t_i_o_n_.

       As another example, use the following command to run on port 9000:

              $$ jjwweebbsseerrvveerr --pp 99000000

       By  default,  the files of the current directory are served.  A different directory can be
       specified with the --dd option.

       By default, every request is logged on the console.  The output looks like this:

              112277..00..00..11 -- -- [[1100//FFeebb//22002211::1144::3344::1111 ++00000000]] ""GGEETT //ssoommee//ssuubbddiirreeccttoorryy// HHTTTTPP//11..11"" 220000 --

       Logging output can be changed with the --oo option.  The default setting is iinnffoo.  The  vveerr--
       bboossee  setting  additionally  includes  the request and response headers as well as the ab-
       solute path of the requested resource.

SSTTOOPPPPIINNGG TTHHEE SSEERRVVEERR
       Once started successfully, the server runs until it is stopped.  On  Unix  platforms,  the
       server can be stopped by sending it a SSIIGGIINNTT signal (CCttrrll++CC in a terminal window).

HHEELLPP OOPPTTIIOONN
       The  --hh  option  displays a help message describing the usage and the options of the jjwweebb--
       sseerrvveerr.
